the burden of HIV/AIDS in the EMR increased from 1990 to2015.

HIV/AIDS mortality and morbidity in Eastern Mediterranean countries increased since 1990, and that this increase is likely to continue in the future unless urgent measures are taken to reverse the trends.

the rate of deaths from HIV/AIDS in the EMR increased by 43%, from 0.3 (0,2–0.9) per 100 000 population in 1990, to 1.8 per 100 00 in 2015, with a corresponding 43% increase in the rate of YLD, from 1.4 per 100 0 population in 1999 to 4.5 in 2015.

the impact of the global HIV/AIDS pandemic in the EMR.
the impact of HIV/AIDS on the population of EMR countries between 1999 and 2015, using the Global Burden Study 2015.
the impact of HIV/AIDS on the health and economic development in the EMR countries.

HIV/AIDS burden in the EMR increased between 1990 to2015, and the increase is due to the increased number of people living with HIV/AIDS, and the increased number of HIV/AIDS-related deaths.

HIV/AIDS morbidity increased in the EMRO region since 1990 and this increase is reflected in the increase in the YLDs and YLLs.

The main takeaway from our work is that

HIV/AIDS morbidity, mortality, and YLLs increased in the Eastern Mediterranean Region (the EMR) between 1990–1994 and 2015, and that the rate of YLD due to HIV/AIDS in the EMR increased between 1990 to the mid-1990s and then decreased in the late 1990s and the early 2000s before increasing again.
HIV morbidity and mortality has been increasing in the EMR countries.
despite the significant progress in reducing mortality and morbidity from HIV/AIDS, HIV/AIDS remains a major health problem in EMR countries.
